title: A move that throws over the game WebSocket kills the server-side game session
expected: WS move path calls `session.engine.executeMove(...)` at apps/riftbound-app/server/ws-game.ts:90 with no try/catch (nor any in server.ts:98-115 websocket.message). In the engine, `checkMoveCondition` runs at packages/core/src/engine/rule-engine.ts:414, OUTSIDE the try block that starts at rule-engine.ts:567, so a throwing move condition escapes executeMove entirely. Empirically verified on the installed Bun 1.3.13: an uncaught throw in Bun.serve `fetch` yields HTTP 500 and the process survives, but an uncaught throw in `websocket.message` terminates the process (exit=1). Process death drops the socket (ERR_CONNECTION_RESET) and wipes the in-memory `gameSessions` map, so after restart GET /api/game/:id/state and WS upgrade (ws-game.ts:26) return 'Game not found'/404 — exactly the observed asymmetry vs REST.
observed: Sending the same Defy playSpell via the browser WS (executeMove) -> net::ERR_CONNECTION_RESET on the socket, then GET /api/game/<id>/state returns 'Game not found' and WS reconnect gets 404; window.__rbGameId becomes null. Via REST the game survived the 500. Reproduced 3 times.
